reason: This passage (Genesis 27) is narrated in omniscient third-person perspective, providing access to the internal thoughts and motivations of Isaac, Rebekah, Jacob, and Esau—all members of a wealthy patriarchal family of high social standing. The narrative focuses on their intimate family drama regarding inheritance and blessings. While Esau is described as a hunter ('אִישׁ שָׂעִר' - a man of the field), the story is not told from the perspective of working people or laborers. Rather, it centers on the privileged concerns and private deliberations of patriarchs and heirs. Working people or servants are entirely absent from the narrative perspective.
